transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um, I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my face. The left side of it, specifically. It looks really crooked and... just messed up. 

It's constantly on my mind. Whenever I'm at work at the warehouse, or even if I try to go out to salsa night, I just feel like everyone is staring at it and noticing how off it is. People tell me they don't see anything when I bring it up, but I know what I see, and I just can't stop fixating on it. It's really taking a toll on me.

When people tell you they don't notice anything different about your face, is there any part of you that considers they might be right, or are you completely certain that your face really is crooked and messed up?

Honestly... no. I don't think they're right at all. I mean, I look in the mirror, and it's just... it's right there. The left side is definitely crooked. I'm completely certain about it. 

When people tell me they don't notice it, I just figure they're trying to be polite, or maybe they just don't want to make me feel bad. But I know what I'm looking at. It really is messed up.
Aside from your concerns about your face, have you noticed any other unusual beliefs or experiences—like feeling people are plotting against you, or hearing/seeing things others don't?

No, I don't have anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, and I don't think anyone is plotting against me. It's really just... just my face that I'm dealing with. That's the only thing that's bothering me.

Do you find yourself doing certain things repeatedly because of how your face looks—like checking it in mirrors, trying to cover or fix that side of your face, or asking others to reassure you about it?

Yeah, I do. Especially at work. Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I always end up in the bathroom checking the mirror. I just keep looking at it, trying to pull my cap down a certain way to hide it, or rubbing at the left side of my face like I can somehow fix it. 

I get stuck doing it. Sometimes I'm in there so long that I end up late getting back out, and my picking numbers fall way behind. My boss has been getting on my case about it a lot lately. But I just can't stop checking it.
Aside from concerns about how your face looks, have you had any other fixed beliefs about your body—like something being wrong internally, a foul smell, or a bodily function not working right?

No, nothing like that. I don't... I don't think I smell bad or have anything wrong on the inside. Everything else with my body works fine. It really is just my face. That's the only thing I'm worried about.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a persistent, distressing preoccupation with a perceived defect (crooked left side of face) that is not observable to others, accompanied by repetitive checking, camouflaging, and reassurance-seeking behaviors. The preoccupation is held with absent insight/delusional conviction (patient is 'completely certain' despite others' feedback), but there are no other psychotic symptoms (no hallucinations, no paranoid ideation, no disorganized thought), and the delusional belief is content-specific to appearance, consistent with Body Dysmorphic Disorder with absent insight/delusional beliefs rather than a primary psychotic disorder. Functional impairment is evident (work performance affected, social avoidance).

confirmed_symptoms: Persistent preoccupation with perceived crookedness/deformity of left side of face
Belief not corroborated by others (defect not observable)
Camouflaging behavior (adjusting cap to hide face)
Repetitive touching/rubbing of the affected area
Patient expresses complete certainty that the defect is real
Rejects others' feedback as insincere rather than considering alternative explanation
No doubt or ambivalence about the belief (absent insight/delusional conviction)
Denies other somatic delusions (e.g., internal illness, foul odor)

Repetitive behaviors (checking, camouflaging, touching) performed in response to appearance concerns
